title: African voices.
Global possibility.
hero.description: Connecting foreign policy, enterprise and international relationships with opportunity for Africa’s people.
hero.alt: Delegates at The Education Collaborative convening in Johannesburg.

introduction: Foreign Africa is a forward-looking, not-for-profit social enterprise working across foreign policy, entrepreneurship and economic transformation.

We bridge policy and practice by engaging governments, investors, the African diaspora and entrepreneurs to advance trade, investment and diplomatic policies that support decent jobs, in line with SDG 8.
Our approach combines policy research with practical initiatives that help African youth and communities participate in the global economy.
mission: To empower Africa’s next generation by shaping international partnerships and foreign policy practices that support sustainable jobs and social entrepreneurship.
We connect diplomatic missions, governments, strategic investors and young innovators to help shape a more competitive and equitable economic future.
payload.vision: A globally competitive Africa powered by sustainable jobs, scalable entrepreneurship and foreign policy shaped by African voices.

values.title: Empowerment
values.text: Enabling Africans, especially youth and women, to use entrepreneurship as a pathway to prosperity.

values.title: Innovation
values.text: Promoting creative solutions that link foreign policy with local economic impact.

values.title: Collaboration

values.title: Integrity

values.title: Inclusivity
values.text: Ensuring diverse voices influence Africa’s global economic positioning.

payload.name: Prof. DeBrenna LaFa Agbényiga
payload.intro: Higher education leadership, international development and community-engaged scholarship.
bio: Professor DeBrenna LaFa Agbényiga, Ph.D., MBA, MSW, serves as Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs at the International University of Grand-Bassam (IUGB), an institution of excellence delivering American-style education in francophone West Africa. With nearly 30 years in higher education administration across diverse institutions including R1 research universities, Hispanic-Serving Institutions, HBCUs, and religious-affiliated colleges, she has advanced diversity, equity, inclusion, student success, accreditation, global education, and strategic planning.

Professor Agbényiga oversees IUGB’s academic enterprise, including schools, faculty development, recruitment, enrollment, retention, student life, and research, while navigating institutional culture within Côte d’Ivoire’s context to drive economic impact. Previously, she held provost roles at Stonehill College and Bowie State University; Vice Provost and Dean of the Graduate School at the University of Texas at San Antonio (UTSA), where she pioneered the first Graduate Student Success Center, implemented Salesforce CRM to enhance graduate recruitment, advising, and experience; associate dean positions at Michigan State University (MSU); and leadership in equity and inclusion initiatives. At UTSA, she drove new graduate programs, supported doctoral expansion toward R1 status, served on key committees, and collaborated with the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board (THECB).

Professor Agbényiga brings extensive experience with U.S. regional accreditors including the Higher Learning Commission (HLC), New England Commission of Higher Education (NECHE), and Middle States Commission on Higher Education (MSCHE). She has also managed discipline-specific accreditation processes for the Council on Social Work Education (CSWE), Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET), Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB), and Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP).

Her scholarship examines organizational culture, international development, entrepreneurship, community sustainability, women’s and children’s rights, gender-based violence, cross-cultural learning, refugee and immigrant resettlement, and social integration. Notable publications include “Expanding our community: independent and interdependent factors impacting refugee successful community resettlement” (Advances in Social Work, 2012), “Linguistic isolation, social capital, and immigrant belonging” (Journal of Contemporary Ethnography, 2012), and “Utilizing social work skills to enhance entrepreneurship training for women: A Ghanaian perspective” (Journal of Community Practice, 2008). She has co-edited books like Children’s Rights in Ghana: Reality or Rhetoric? (Lexington Books, 2011) and contributed chapters to Springer volumes on vulnerable children. Most recently, she has a forthcoming article examining Ethics and Leadership in a West Africa Higher Education Context. Currently, she is leading the Giving Voice to Values for Students French project. The project includes translating the program from English to French and designing ethical dilemma case studies in the francophone context.

Professor Agbényiga has led study abroad programs in Ghana and Jamaica and has spent years working across Western, Eastern, and Southern Africa as a researcher and consultant to ministries, NGOs, and universities. Her work has also included projects and collaborations in Ghana, Togo, South Africa, Tanzania, Namibia, Nigeria, Jamaica, and Côte d’Ivoire reflecting a sustained commitment to Africa and diaspora partnerships. These experiences strengthen her broader focus on international education, cross-cultural learning, and community-engaged scholarship.

Professor Agbényiga contributes philanthropically as Board Member of the Opoku Ware School (Ghana) Endowment Fund, Advisory Board Chair for Curriculum Modernization and International Experience Design for the African Diaspora Nation, and past member of National Coalition of 100 Black Women chapters. Current roles include Appointed Chair and Member of the Advisory Council for Foreign Africa, Member of the Board of Directors for the African Council on Foreign Relations (ACFR), Founding Ambassador for the Global Funding Team of the 250X2040 Initiative, and Reviewer for the Ghana Journal of Higher Education Management. She has also served on various committees for the Council on Social Work Education (CSWE), advancing global social work education and curricula.

She holds a Ph.D. and MSW in Social Work (Urban Studies), plus an MBA in Integrative Strategic Management, all from Michigan State University, and a B.A. in Criminal Justice with a Sociology minor from the University of South Carolina.

Professor Agbényiga is married to Mr. Agbeko Kokou Agbényiga, a long-time educator and advocate for students. They have two daughters, Gabrielle Mama Aku Sika Agbényiga, an alumna of St. Catherine University and a recent graduate with her Master of Development Practice with a focus on International Development from the Humphrey School of Public Affairs at the University of Minnesota. Their daughter, Emmanuella Nana Yaa Konadu Brefo is in her second year at St. Catherine University studying International Studies and Women and International Development.

payload.name: Alhaji Mikdad Mohammed
payload.intro: Economic diplomacy, strategic partnerships, investment and energy policy.
bio: Mikdad Mohammed is an economic diplomacy, partnerships, investment, and energy policy professional with expertise in deal structuring, investment facilitation, climate finance, strategic partnerships and development cooperation.

He currently serves as Head of Partnerships and Investment at the Energy Commission of Ghana, where he leads the Commission’s engagement with development partners, investors, and bilateral and multilateral institutions to mobilise strategic partnerships, investment, and climate finance in support of Ghana’s energy transition agenda.

Prior to joining the Energy Commission, Mikdad served as Senior Economic and Commercial Specialist Advisor at the Embassy of the United Arab Emirates in Accra, advising on trade, investment, and bilateral relations in Ghana, Togo, and São Tomé and Príncipe. During his tenure, UAE–Ghana bilateral trade grew from US$2.1 billion in 2019 to over US$7 billion by the end of 2025. He managed over US$16 million in UAE humanitarian programs and projects across Ghana and Togo over six years, and played a pivotal role in facilitating the UAE’s US$30 million climate resilience grant to Ghana post-COP28. He also served as the UAE’s local focal person for COP28 for Ghana, Togo and São Tomé, coordinating stakeholder engagement in support of the UAE’s climate diplomacy initiatives.

Before joining the Emirati Embassy, Mikdad worked with the Institute for Energy Security (IES), where he rose to Senior Research and Policy Analyst, having started his professional career at Ghana’s state-owned BOST Energies.

Mikdad holds a Master of Economic Policy Management from the University of Ghana, Legon, and has undertaken executive training with the Abu Dhabi Investment Office (ADIO) and the Dubai International Chamber of Commerce in investment promotion and international trade.
He is married with two children.

payload.name: Mushara Amidu Koriwie
payload.intro: Operations, organisational management and private-sector implementation.
bio: Mushara Amidu Koriwie is an operations and property management professional with experience spanning Ghana and the United Kingdom, working across facilities management, business development, financial administration, client relations, and organisational coordination.

She has held operational and supervisory roles with PB Smart Facilities Management in London, Goldkey Properties Limited, and Devtraco Plus Limited in Accra. Across these roles, she has managed commercial and residential property portfolios, coordinated multidisciplinary teams, overseen budgets and service delivery, and supported the development of efficient operational systems. Her professional experience has given her a practical understanding of how organisations translate strategy into effective delivery across different institutional and cultural environments.

Mushara holds an International MBA with Professional Placement from Birmingham City University, United Kingdom, and a BSc in Land Economy from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Ghana.

As a member of Foreign Africa’s Advisory Council, she brings expertise in operations, organisational management, property and facilities systems, business development, and client engagement. Her experience across both markets contributes a valuable private-sector and implementation perspective to the Council’s role in supporting Foreign Africa’s institutional development and long-term growth.

payload.name: Elorm Mawuli-Kwawu
payload.intro: African regional integration, diplomacy, institutional development and policy implementation.
bio: Elorm Mawuli-Kwawu is an Africa-focused International Relations and Development Policy Researcher whose work covers African regional integration, diplomacy, institutional development, and policy implementation. With over a decade of experience across research, multi-country programming, and international cooperation, Elorm combines policy and practice, focusing on how African institutions translate regional and continental ambitions into effective partnerships, programmes, and development outcomes. As Head of Global Engagements at Foreign Africa, he leads institutional building, research and strategic partnerships, anchoring the organisation’s external positioning and policy work across Africa and internationally.

Elorm has coordinated programme delivery across multiple Southern African Development Community (SADC) Member States with Open Society Initiative for Southern Africa (OSISA), aligning implementation with regional policy frameworks and strengthening governance systems for planning, risk monitoring, and reporting. He also delivered multi-country political economy and security risk analysis under the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (UK-FCDO) Sahel Initiative, producing high-level briefs for senior decision-makers and improving programme coordination through structured tracking and reporting systems.

In 2022, Elorm led cross-regional facilitation as Africa Engagement Lead for the Saudi-funded Misk Foundation, coordinating partnerships across Africa and the Gulf and supporting leadership teams. Elorm previously served as Consulting Head of Research and Communications at the All-Africa Students Union (AASU), directing research and policy engagement across a pan-African network, coordinating multi-country programmes, and producing institutional outputs for engagement with the African Union (AU) and Regional Economic Communities (RECs).

Earlier, as a Research Assistant in Ghana’s Parliament, he produced policy briefs and analytical reports to support legislative decision-making and coordinated stakeholder engagement. Alongside his policy work, Elorm serves as an Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Media, Arts and Communication (UNIMAC), where he teaches and supervises students.

Elorm is a NUPI-certified Trainer of Trainers (ToT) with the African Centre for the Constructive Resolution of Disputes (ACCORD) in South Africa, delivering capacity-building programmes in governance, negotiation, leadership and strategic facilitation. Elorm contributes to academic and policy discourse through publications, conference presentations, and collaborative research on governance and regional integration. His work has been presented at international forums across Africa and Europe. In recognition of his contributions to cross-regional engagement and policy dialogues, he was awarded the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) grant in 2025 to support his participation in a high-level Africa–Europe Cooperation forum at the Khel University of Applied Sciences in Germany and policy engagements at the European Union (EU) Parliament in Strasbourg, France.

payload.name: Rita Abla Dugbenu
payload.intro: Development, learning and project management supporting women, youth and institutional capacity.
bio: Rita Abla Dugbenu is a development professional, learning expert, and project management specialist with over eight years of experience designing, managing, and implementing projects focused on education, women and adolescent development, child rights, youth transitions, sustainable livelihoods, and human capital development in Africa.

She currently serves as the Assistant Director, West Africa Hub at The Education Collaborative, Ashesi University, where she works closely with the Executive Director and regional committees to expand The Collaborative’s footprint and strengthen networks across West Africa. In this role, she oversees the design and implementation of hub initiatives, manages engagement with member institutions, coordinates impact tracking and reporting, and facilitates collaborations that enhance institutional capacity and advance student success across the region.

Rita has also led impactful programs supporting women and youth through her work with International Needs Ghana and the Gender Centre for Empowering Development (GenCED). She remains deeply committed to advancing gender equity, youth empowerment, and community development across Africa.
Rita holds a BA in Spanish and Linguistics and an MA in International Affairs from the University of Ghana.

payload.name: Rexford Akrong
payload.intro: International development, agricultural economics, sustainability and monitoring and evaluation.
bio: Rexford Akrong is an international development practitioner and researcher with expertise in agricultural economics, sustainability, and programme implementation across West and Southern Africa. His work focuses on education and agriculture, with broader interests in youth and women’s empowerment, digitalisation, rural and urban development, migration, and natural resource management.

He has supported the design and implementation of development and poverty-alleviation programmes, including work in monitoring and evaluation for education and digital rights initiatives. He has developed monitoring and evaluation frameworks to track programme performance and assess impact, and has experience managing large-scale research projects in the education and agriculture sectors.
Rexford has worked closely with government agencies and ministries to implement development programmes, contributing to policy and programme delivery in multiple national contexts.

He holds a Bachelor’s degree in Economics from the University of Cape Coast, a Master of Science in Agricultural and Applied Economics from the University of Nairobi, and a Doctor of Philosophy in Development Studies from the University of Cape Coast.

payload.name: Nana Osei Agyekum
payload.intro: Strategic communications, institutional partnerships and cross-border mobility in Africa.
bio: Nana Osei Agyekum is a strategic communications professional with nearly a decade of experience across corporate communications, business development, institutional partnerships and cross-border mobility in Africa. At Foreign Africa, he serves as the organisation’s communications strategist, translating research, programmes and partnerships into clear public and institutional engagement, with a practical grounding in how mobility systems, visa regimes and institutional coordination shape the movement of people and organisations across the continent.

He currently serves as Head of Communications, Sales and Marketing at Travel Desk Limited, where he leads corporate communications, commercial strategy, brand development and institutional partnerships within the corporate travel and MICE ecosystem. Based in Accra, Ghana, Nana has managed visa advisory and mobility arrangements, supporting more than 1,200 multi-country deployments across more than 25 African countries, giving him direct exposure to the regulatory, stakeholder, and cross-border coordination realities that continue to shape mobility within Africa.

Previously, as Business Development Manager at TravelPass Limited, Nana managed institutional relationships and business operations while contributing to the digitalisation of internal processes. Earlier, at Satguru Travels Limited, he supported business development and corporate communications, contributing to institutional engagements involving organisations including UNICEF, JICA, Deloitte, MTN and CEIBS.

At Foreign Africa, Nana brings this combination of communications expertise, private-sector experience and practical knowledge of cross-border mobility to the organisation’s continental work and strategic communications positioning. His perspective is particularly relevant to Foreign Africa’s interests in regional integration, cross-border movement, enterprise connectivity, and institutional engagement — offering insight into the regulatory and administrative barriers that individuals, businesses and institutions encounter when attempting to operate across national boundaries.

payload.name: Abdul Karim Ibrahim
payload.intro: Broadcast journalism, policy research, public narratives and global health diplomacy.
bio: Abdul Karim Ibrahim is a Ghanaian broadcast journalist and researcher with experience in development collaboration and global policy engagement. He has worked in various capacities including as Africa Regional Consultant for the UNITE Parliamentarians Network for Global Health, based in Lisbon. His expertise covers policy research, legislative mobilization, and global health diplomacy. He has successfully supported collaborations with global partners including the World Health Organization (WHO), Global Fund, Africa CDC, Wellcome Trust, UNITAID, and engagements linked to the World Health Assembly, contributing to the advancement of African priorities within global health governance processes.

He is a recipient of the CODESRIA African Research in Indigenous and Alternative Knowledges (AFRIAK) Fellowship for early career researchers. His research interests span cultural infrastructure in African cities; the politics of football as a lens for understanding post-independence development trajectories; youth and platform-based work in Ghana; and questions of state capacity and social protection.

In 2023, he was affiliated with the Arnold-Bergstraesser-Institut at the University of Freiburg, Germany, and the Institute of African Studies, University of Ghana, where he contributed to a transregional research project on decolonization in higher education. He is also a contributor and Africa Regional Editor to The Bloomsbury Handbook of Student Politics and Representation in Higher Education (2024).

Karim is a member of the Council for the Development of Social Science Research in Africa, Dakar. He is also a longstanding member of Speech Forces, where he has trained over 5,000 students across secondary and tertiary institutions in debate, critical thinking, and public communication across multiple African countries.

payload.name: Emmanuel Nuvi Junior
payload.intro: Education programming, language learning, youth development and international collaboration.
bio: Emmanuel Nuvi Junior is a development-oriented education professional and language learning specialist with over five years of experience in curriculum design, pedagogy, and international education programming. His work sits at the intersection of education, youth development, and human capital development, with a strong focus on language as a tool for social mobility and inclusive development.

He has worked extensively with Alliance Française, where he contributed to the creation of language teaching content and methodologies aimed at improving learner engagement, communicative competence, and access to quality language education. His experience includes developing instructional materials, supporting teacher practice, and promoting innovative, learner-centred approaches to language acquisition.

Currently serving as an English Language Assistant in France, Emmanuel supports student-centred learning within public education institutions while contributing to intercultural exchange and academic mobility. He has also co-authored research in the field of education, with a focus on student leadership in Ghanaian Universities. Emmanuel holds a Bachelor of Education in Arts (English and French) from the University of Cape Coast and a Master’s degree in International Affairs from the University of Ghana. He is committed to advancing education-led development, youth empowerment, and Africa-focused policy and practice through research, programming, and international collaboration.

payload.name: James Kodjie
payload.intro: Youth empowerment, democratic governance, education and Pan-African policy engagement.
bio: James Kodjie is a development practitioner and policy researcher with experience in youth empowerment, democratic governance, education, and Pan-African engagement. He has a strong background in programme coordination and stakeholder mobilisation, with a focus on multi-country initiatives and policy engagement.

He has coordinated regional campaigns and policy initiatives, including work on digital inclusion in Southern Africa and youth engagement platforms linked to continental policy processes. He has also contributed to the development of governance assessment frameworks for tertiary institutions and policy actors across Africa.

His work includes data-driven policy research, with experience in analysing and synthesising socio-political issues to inform programme design and advocacy. He has contributed to international policy discourse, including co-authoring a chapter in The Bloomsbury Handbook of Student Politics and Representation in Higher Education.
James holds a Bachelor of Arts in Integrated Development Studies and a Master of Science in Development Studies. He is currently a doctoral candidate in Interdisciplinary Studies.
His work focuses on strengthening governance systems, advancing education policy, and supporting youth participation in decision-making processes across Africa.

payload.summary: Following its Ethiopia and Rwanda mission, Foreign Africa has entered a structured 90-day phase to turn priority conversations into research, pilot activities and institutional workstreams.
paragraphs: Foreign Africa has concluded its Continental Institutional Engagement Mission to Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, and Kigali, Rwanda. Led by Founder and Head of Global Engagement Elorm Mawuli-Kwawu, the August 2026 mission connected diplomacy and continental policy with research, higher education and enterprise development.

In Addis Ababa, discussions with the Embassy of Ghana explored policy research supporting Ghana’s continental diplomatic engagement. At the African Union Commission’s Department of Economic Development, Tourism, Trade, Industry and Minerals (ETTIM), dialogue covered trade, industrialisation, enterprise development and regional integration, including a prospective AU-related engagement in January 2027.

Engagement with UNDP Africa identified alignment around the Africa Trade and Jobs Tracker, Junior Associates Programme, Enterprise Development Workshop Series and Timbuktoo Initiative. Discussions with the Institute for Security Studies explored regional integration, governance, municipal diplomacy and entrepreneurial diplomacy.

In Kigali, African Leadership University and its Centre for Entrepreneurial Leadership identified potential collaboration on youth employment, applied research, enterprise development and the Africa Trade and Jobs Tracker. ALU requested a formal proposal setting out specific areas for institutional collaboration.

Foreign Africa also engaged Westerwelle Startup Haus Kigali on founder development and connections to Accra. The Ghana High Commission provided diplomatic and institutional guidance. A channel was opened for formal engagement with Rwanda Development Board, alongside initial contact with Norrsken House Kigali.

The structured 90-day follow-up phase focuses on converting priority engagements into defined workstreams, research outputs, pilot activities and longer-term relationships. Initial engagements, identified opportunities, agreed actions and formal partnerships remain distinct stages.

payload.summary: Foreign Africa joined university leaders, practitioners and partners at The Education Collaborative’s inaugural Southern African Convening.
paragraphs: Foreign Africa began its working year with an engagement in Johannesburg at The Education Collaborative’s inaugural Southern African Convening, bringing together university leaders, practitioners and partners focused on research development and social impact.

The organisation was represented by its Head of Global Engagements, Board Chair Professor De Brenna, Provost and Vice President of Academic Affairs at the University of Grand-Bassam in Côte d’Ivoire, and Abla, Programmes and Partnerships Lead.

The convening offered a platform for exchanging ideas, building relationships and exploring collaboration on research, programme development and institutional partnerships. This participation forms part of Foreign Africa’s effort to strengthen academic networks across the continent.

payload.summary: A registration snapshot from the first four Enterprise Development Workshop Series sessions shows demand for practical enterprise skills.
paragraphs: Foreign Africa’s published EDWS registration snapshot reports 474 registrations across the first four sessions, with 25 countries represented and 2,567 registration-page views.
These figures describe registrations and page views. They do not establish unique participants, attendance, completion rates or jobs created.

Among registrants who shared their business stage, 70% were at the idea or early stage. The snapshot also reports that 47 of 67 Session 4 registrants had not yet engaged investors, donors or government.
The findings point to a practical need for enterprise skills, structure and access to institutional and funding networks.

payload.summary: The Kigali mission brought discussions with entrepreneurship hubs, diplomatic networks and higher education into one programme of engagement.
paragraphs: Foreign Africa’s Kigali mission update describes engagement across higher education, entrepreneurship hubs and diplomatic institutions as part of its Continental Institutional Engagement Mission.
At Westerwelle Startup Haus Kigali, the focus included founder networks, mentorship and enterprise ecosystems, with discussion of pathways connecting to Accra.

The update also identifies engagement with the Ghana High Commission in Kigali on economic diplomacy and institutional access, and with African Leadership University on the Junior Associates Programme and entrepreneurial leadership.
The mission update also names Rwanda Development Board and ecosystem hubs in discussions about future investment, regional integration and trade-driven employment.

payload.summary: Foreign Africa’s Addis Ababa update outlines discussions with UNDP Africa around trade, enterprise development and opportunities for junior associates.
paragraphs: The Addis Ababa phase of Foreign Africa’s Continental Institutional Engagement Mission included reported engagement with Barbara Asamoah and the UNDP Africa Region Office team.

Foreign Africa’s update identifies four pathways for prospective collaboration: the Africa Trade and Jobs Tracker, the Timbuktoo Project, the Junior Associates Programme and the Enterprise Development Workshop Series.
The post also describes a prospective pathway for Junior Associates to access UNDP’s Senior Fellows Programme. It does not establish an open application call or guarantee eligibility or placement.
The mission connects Foreign Africa’s focus on trade, policy and enterprise with institutional dialogue, bringing its programmes into conversations about Africa’s economic development.

payload.title: Beyond the Logo: Building Brands Investors and Governments Trust

photo.alt: EDWS Session 4 announcement: Beyond the Logo, featuring Dr. Temitope Falade and facilitator Hildana Mesai, 9 October 2026.

payload.summary: EDWS Session 4 focused on the relationship between brand credibility, investor confidence and institutional trust.
paragraphs: Foreign Africa’s Session 4 announcement scheduled “Beyond the Logo: Building Brands Investors and Governments Trust” for 9 October 2026, from 3:00 to 4:30 PM GMT on Microsoft Teams.

The announcement named Dr. Temitope Falade as speaker and Hildana Mesai as facilitator. The speaker spotlight introduced Dr. Falade as Head of Brands, Communications and Marketing at Pan-Atlantic University, Lagos.
The stated themes included executive communications, reputation and crisis management, brand governance, digital engagement and storytelling that builds stakeholder trust.
The announced session brought brand credibility and institutional trust into EDWS’s practical enterprise-learning agenda.
